steps.title: Deep unsupervised learning using nonequilibrium thermodynamics
steps.teaches: Diffusion probabilistic models: defining a forward diffusion process that gradually destroys data and learning a reverse process to generate data, trained via variational inference.

steps.title: The Logic of Least Squares
steps.teaches: Foundations of least squares estimation, including mean square error and unbiasedness.
steps.why_here: The target paper contrasts ridge regression with ordinary least squares; without understanding least squares logic, the bias-variance tradeoff and motivation for biased estimation are unclear.

steps.title: Solving systems of linear equations with a positive definite, symmetric, but possibly ill-conditioned matrix
steps.teaches: Numerical difficulties in solving ill-conditioned positive definite linear systems, such as those arising from nonorthogonal predictors.
steps.why_here: Ridge regression adds a constant to the diagonal of X'X to improve conditioning; this reference explains why ill-conditioning makes least squares estimates unstable.

steps.title: Applied Statistical Decision Theory.
steps.teaches: Decision-theoretic framework for estimation, including loss functions and Bayes rules.
steps.why_here: The target paper evaluates estimators by mean squared error and advocates biased estimation; decision theory provides the formal basis for comparing biased and unbiased estimators.

steps.title: Confidence Sets for the Mean of a Multivariate Normal Distribution
steps.teaches: Inadmissibility of the sample mean in high dimensions and improved confidence sets via shrinkage.
steps.why_here: This is a key theoretical result showing that biased (shrinkage) estimators can dominate unbiased ones, directly motivating ridge regression's biased approach.
